The operating model

Clear allocations.
Shorter paths to the work.

Our aim is to reduce administrative delay while sustaining rigorous research and meaningful opportunities for graduate students. The framework below is a proposal: allocation amounts, approval deadlines, and legal terms must be agreed for each project. It does not announce fixed institutional percentages.

Budget student support first.

Identify graduate-student roles, paid research time, supervision, and any tuition or benefits before committing the rest of the budget. Give this support its own allocation and payment plan, so students can see what is funded and for how long. Student payments must use the appropriate appointment, payroll, fellowship, or other permitted process.

Make every allocation visible.

Divide the project budget into graduate-student support, investigator and research-team compensation, other direct project costs, and administration or indirect costs. The amounts must add up to the agreed total. These are spending allocations, not automatic cash distributions or promised returns. Each charge needs a documented project purpose.

Agree the route before work starts.

Name a budget approver and an academic supervisor. Set the approval turnaround, the time to process an approved payment once funds and documentation are available, and the sponsor’s invoice deadline. Agree an advance or milestone schedule that can support those commitments. A clear route reduces repeated negotiations and gives delayed requests an accountable owner.

Track progress and adjust openly.

Review spending, upcoming student commitments, and deliverables together. Document budget changes and obtain any required sponsor consent before reallocating funds. Neither a short approval target nor a late sponsor payment removes existing obligations to students or employees. If funding is delayed, communicate promptly and agree what work can continue.

Grants and contracts have different constraints.

A commercial contract sets an agreed price and scope. A sponsored research award may restrict eligible costs, indirect costs, student appointments, reporting, and transfers between budget categories. Award conditions and applicable law govern those decisions. For U.S. federal awards, see the official cost principles in 2 CFR Part 200, Subpart E. Other funders and jurisdictions may use different rules.

01 / Agreement and project

Identify the agreement and its duration. Dates are entered explicitly; no agreement is signed by this form.

Identify the award, version/date, restrictions, reporting, and required flow-down terms. Include the operative requirements or identify the documents both parties will receive. This draft does not replace a sponsor’s award instrument.
02 / The parties

Use the actual legal entities and authorized signatories, not just trading names. Notice addresses appear in the agreement.

Enter the full registered name of the entity signing for BIOracle.
03 / Scope and delivery

Be specific enough for both parties to know what work is included, when it is due, and how it will be assessed.

State the review deadline, objective criteria, rejection procedure, and any correction period.
04 / Funding and allocation

Budget details are optional. Use a decimal point and no thousands separators. When all allocations and the total are supplied, they must balance.

Enter an allocation if agreed; otherwise the PDF marks student support as to be agreed.
Specify advance or milestone amounts and dates, invoice triggers, and any final reconciliation or refund arrangements.
05 / Graduate-student support

Define the funded commitments and who is responsible for them. Do not enter bank details, tax identifiers, or other sensitive personal information.

Include number of students or roles, period and rate of support, tuition/benefits if applicable, appointment or payment mechanism, payment dates, supervision, and how existing commitments are handled if funding is delayed.
06 / Rights and legal terms

These provisions depend on the parties, jurisdiction, and sponsor. Specify the intended terms; obtain legal review before signature.

Identify the agreed court location and jurisdiction; this template uses negotiation followed by court proceedings.
Identify background IP, third-party restrictions, invention rights, and any agreed licenses. Missing terms remain to be agreed.
Specify publication rights, sponsor review periods, confidentiality or patent delays, and student thesis rights.
Describe permitted data, access, retention/deletion, incident notification, and applicable privacy or ethics requirements. Enter “No personal or regulated data permitted” if appropriate.
Enter an agreed positive cap in the project currency, or leave blank for a to-be-agreed placeholder.
Identify any clause being modified. Do not include signatures or sensitive credentials.
